# Parse Track XML Instead of tTrackSeg

**Decision.** Reconstruct the track centreline **offline, by parsing the track's XML definition**,
instead of reading TORCS's own `tTrackSeg` geometry at runtime.

**Date.** Recorded in `guide.txt` §0, published 2026-07-10. The work it governs
(`racing_line.py`) predates publication — the branch it comes from has upstream commits from
2026-04-19 onward, and the generated racing line is dated 2026-06-04/05.

## The rejected alternative, and why it fails

The original plan said to relax the racing line along `tTrackSeg` coordinates — the natural choice,
since that is the simulator's own internal representation of the track. It is unreachable:

> "The plan says 'run the relaxation along the tTrackSeg coordinates.' `tTrackSeg` is a TORCS C++
> runtime structure. It is ONLY visible to a robot compiled inside TORCS. Our agent talks to TORCS
> over the SCR UDP protocol (snakeoil3_gym.py) and CANNOT see tTrackSeg."
> — IT Applications in Business and Commerce/project/code/a.bhuiyan/guide.txt, 2026-07-10

Taking `tTrackSeg` would have meant abandoning [[torcs-scr-protocol]] and compiling the agent into
the simulator as a C++ robot — which would also mean abandoning Python, [[pytorch]] and the entire
training stack. The alternative was rejected on reachability, not on quality.

## What replaced it

> "Fix: get the identical geometry OFFLINE by parsing the track XML
> (torcs/tracks/road/<track>/<track>.xml). It encodes the track as an ordered list of segments:
> straights (lg) and arcs (radius, arc, lft/rgt). Integrate those to rebuild the centerline, then
> relax. Same math, a source we can actually reach from Python."
> — IT Applications in Business and Commerce/project/code/a.bhuiyan/guide.txt, 2026-07-10

`racing_line.py` (507 lines) does exactly that: arc-length integration over straights and arcs
including clothoid transitions (`r0`/`r1`), then periodic Laplacian relaxation inside a
`±(w/2 − 1.5 m)` corridor. See [[minimum-curvature-racing-line]].

Runtime localisation then uses only sensors the UDP protocol *does* expose — `distFromStart` as arc
length, `trackPos` as lateral offset, `angle` as heading error, `speedX` as speed. The precomputed
line becomes a lookup keyed on `distFromStart`, which is what makes the tracking-error state of
[[residual-reinforcement-learning]] possible at all.

## The consequence nobody planned: this became the house style

Having established that vendor XML is the reachable source of truth, the same move was applied to the
car. `car_spec.py` walks `practice.xml` → `scr_server.xml` → the car XML to pull gear ratios, final
drive, tyre radius, the rpm→torque curve and the rev limiter — see
[[data-driven-gearing-over-hand-tuned-rpm-bands]]. Two independent subsystems, one technique: **parse
the simulator's configuration files rather than guess at, or try to reach, its runtime state.**

## Costs accepted

- **The line is per-track and precomputed.** Change the track in the TORCS GUI and the `.npz` must be
  regenerated; the guide says so explicitly.
- **Offline geometry has no ground-truth alignment to the runtime `s` origin.** `guide.txt` gotcha G5
  flags that `distFromStart` may not coincide with XML `segment[0]`, and gotcha G4 names a
  `recon_lap.py` calibration tool — **which does not exist in the tree**.

  calibrated is unrecorded, since the tool the guide points at was never committed. `confidence: low`
